messages:
Jordan (oncall): Heads up — monitoring alerted on embeddings API. Error rate for produce_embeddings spiked at 01:13 UTC, many 4xx with message about dimension mismatch. Paging oncall.
embeddings-bot: ALERT: embeddings-v1 error_rate > 5% (5m). link: https://redwood/ops/alerts/embeds-1789
Maya (support): multiple customers opened tickets: acme and searchly report immediate 400s. They pasted error body saying embedding size mismatch (expected 1536 got 768).
Luke (eng-ml): any recent model or batcher deploys? Last model swap was this morning to model-embed-3 (1536 dims).
Rita (sre): pulling pod logs now. I see repeated stack traces in batcher worker:
```\n[2026-03-15T01:12:59Z] ERROR embeddings.worker: ValueError: embedding size 1536 expected, got 768
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/batcher.py\", line 412, in process_batch
    out = kernel.run(concat_inputs)
ValueError: embedding size mismatch
```\nJordan (oncall): Maya, can you paste a sample request payload that produced the 400 so we can repro?
Maya (support): Redacted payload posted to the ticket — simple call via our SDK. Note: many clients still on sdk v0.9.2. They call the public /v1/embeddings endpoint without pinning model version.
Luke (eng-ml): suspect: batcher is combining requests for different model variants, concatenating tensors of differing embedding size. Historically we assumed homogeneous dims in a batch. If some clients request embed-2 (768) and some embed-3 (1536) and the batcher concatenates, kernel throws.
Rita (sre): confirmed. I see headers where x-model is embed-2 and embed-3 in same batch window. The batching code did blind concat when requests came within the same batching tick. No dim validation. Opened an emergency patch to reject mixed-dim batches and to return a clear 422 error.
Jordan (oncall): immediate mitigations:
  1) Disable cross-model batching (set env var BATCH_CROSS_MODEL=false)
  2) Scale up embed-batcher pods by +2 to absorb backlog
  3) Route legacy embed-2 traffic to a separate pool (route-tag: embed-legacy)
Rita (sre): applied BATCH_CROSS_MODEL=false to staging then prod. Triggered rolling restart for batcher pods. deploy-bot reports rolling update started.
deploy-bot: Deploy started by Rita. Branch: batcher/validate-dims. Rolling restart of 5 batcher pods, parallelism 2.
Rita (sre): patch landed and 3/5 pods rolled. Error rate down from 6.2% to 1.8% in the last 2 mins. Still seeing a small tail of 400s from a few dedicated customers.
Maya (support): informing affected customers with short term workaround: either pin model to embed-2 or upgrade SDK to v1.2 which includes correct model metadata. Sending templated note now.
Luke (eng-ml): adding ingress-level validation as follow-up: check model dims in request metadata before batching. If mismatch, return 422 with message explaining expected dims and client SDK link. Also adding a server-side fallback to avoid mixing dims in a single kernel call.
Jordan (oncall): can you add a quick log metric for client SDK version in the next hour? want to know how many callers are using older clients so we can prioritize outreach.
Rita (sre): added short-term metric tag sdk_version to request logs and updated dashboards. Early numbers show ~4% of traffic still low-version.
Maya (support): customers ACME and Searchly confirmed recovery after we asked them to pin model or retry. Both appreciated fast response.
embeddings-bot: Stats update: error_rate now 0.6%  p95 latency 86ms  p99 latency 122ms.
Luke (eng-ml): next steps for postmortem:
  - root cause: batcher assumed homogeneous embedding dimensions; new model launch introduced mixed-dim traffic
  - contributing factors: no ingress schema validation; cross-model batching enabled by default; lack of telemetry for client SDK versions
  - actions: enforce model-dim validation at gateway, default disable cross-model batching, backfill telemetry, add regression test in CI for mixed-model batches
Rita (sre): filing ENG-9872 with RCA and runbook. I'll include rollback plan and the env flag as a quick mitigation step.
Jordan (oncall): I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then hand off to next shift. Thanks everyone.
Maya (support): closing customer escalations as of now, will reopen if they see new errors.
Jordan (oncall): converting thread into an incident ticket and scheduling postmortem doc. Thanks all.
